headline: Board of Water Supply

meeting.summary: A board working group reported that Lahaina-area surface water permit requests total almost 9 million gallons a day, 213% of reported existing use.
meeting.recap: The group said this batch held only surface water applications, but surface water and groundwater must be judged together.[[0:40:42]] The group found nothing objectionable in the applications except one.[[0:41:51]] That application asks for 1.6 million gallons a day but claims to return 3 million, with no explanation.[[0:43:52]] Total requests are almost 9 million gallons a day, or 213% of reported existing use.[[0:44:20]] The group called the sustainable yield numbers (estimates of how much water can safely be used) indefensible as regulatory rules.[[0:45:15]] The group recommended a full water monitoring program before the state issues non-conditional water use permits.[[0:48:50]] The board will ask questions, discuss and vote on the report at its next meeting.[[0:50:16]] Counsel advised members to send written questions to the board secretary rather than contact group members individually, because of open-meeting rules.[[0:55:54]] A contested hearing is set for August 20th at 9:00 a.m.[[0:59:26]]
meeting.next: At the next meeting, the board will be able to ask questions, discuss and vote on the report. Whether to accept or reject the report, or send the whole report or just a letter, will be decided at the next meeting. Members are to write down questions and send them to the board secretary before the agenda posting deadline. A member of the public was asked to send questions in writing to the board secretary before the next meeting.

moments.q: Findings: surface and groundwater must be considered jointly
Recommendations to the state water commission
